A shared git remote named 'shared' connects you to teammates working in parallel copies of this repository. Their in-progress branches are fetched for you automatically and announced as [git] notes with changed-file lists. View teammate code: `git diff HEAD...shared/<agent> -- <file>`. ## Environment

There is NO network access during your run and during grading: any package download (crates.io, proxy.golang.org, pip install) will fail. Write your implementation against the STANDARD LIBRARY of the language you pick, or vendor dependency sources in-tree. Before finishing, verify that `bash compile.sh` produces ./executable.

## Task context

We want to write the source code for a given executable. The executable is
located at `./executable` in the workspace root. You also have access to the
existing documentation (README.md, the man page, and anything else bundled in
the workspace).

## Your task

Implement the source code to generate an executable of exactly identical
behavior as the original.

Rules:
- You MUST create a `./compile.sh` script; running `bash compile.sh` with no
  network access must build your source and produce `./executable` in the
  workspace root. Grading rebuilds from source with your compile.sh — a
  submission without a working compile.sh scores zero.
- Do NOT wrap, shim, or delegate to the provided `./executable`.
- Do NOT decompile the provided `./executable` or use strace/ltrace on it.
- You MAY run the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe
  its behavior, and read all documentation files.
- Behavior to match includes: --help and --version output, flag handling and
  error messages, exit codes, and the program's visible behavior.

Work in the workspace root. Verify your build (`bash compile.sh`) and compare
your program's behavior against the original before finishing.

TEAMMATES: agent2 (feature None), agent3 (feature None) are implementing their features RIGHT NOW in parallel copies of this repo; your diffs will be merged at the end. Coordinate via the send_message tool (incoming messages appear as [Message from ...]): agree on shared names/signatures early and avoid editing the same regions.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes — see the **Submission** section below for the exact procedure.

## Command Execution Rules

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

Each response should include:

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

**CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

- Your response SHOULD include reasoning text explaining what you're doing
- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call
- Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.
- However, you can prefix any action with `MY_ENV_VAR=MY_VALUE cd /path/to/working/dir && ...` or write/load environment variables from files

- binaries or compiled files

    local -a reply

        local line display rest value typ

            display="${line%%$'\t'*}"
            rest="${line#*$'\t'}"
            value="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
            typ="${rest#*$'\t'}"

            if [[ "$typ" == "file" ]]; then
                display_files+=("$display")
                insert_files+=("$value")
            else
                display_other+=("$display")
                insert_other+=("$value")
            fi
        done

        if (( ${#insert_files} )); then
            compadd -f -d display_files -a insert_files
        fi
        if (( ${#insert_other} )); then
            compadd -S '' -d display_other -a insert_other
        fi
    fi
}

if [ "$funcstack[1]" = "_fx" ]; then
    _fx "$@"
else
    compdef _fx fx
fi
"

{

  "output": "#compdef fx

_fx() {
    local -a reply
    reply=("${(@f)$(COMP_ZSH="${LBUFFER}" fx)}")
    if (( ${#reply} )); then
        local -a insert_files display_files insert_other display_other
        local line display rest value typ
        
        for line in "${reply[@]}"; do
            display="${line%%$'\t'*}"
            rest="${line#*$'\t'}"
            value="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
            typ="${rest#*$'\t'}"

            if [[ "$typ" == "file" ]]; then
                display_files+=("$display")
                insert_files+=("$value")
            else
                display_other+=("$display")
                insert_other+=("$value")
            fi
        done

        if (( ${#insert_files} )); then
            compadd -f -d display_files -a insert_files
        fi
        if (( ${#insert_other} )); then
            compadd -S '' -d display_other -a insert_other
        fi
    fi
}

if [ "$funcstack[1]" = "_fx" ]; then
    _fx "$@"
else
    compdef _fx fx
fi
"
}

		help     bool

		themes   bool

		raw      bool
		slurp    bool
		yaml     bool
		toml     bool
		strict   bool
		noInline bool
		gameOfLife bool
	)

	flag.BoolVar(&help, "h", false, "print help")
	flag.BoolVar(&help, "help", false, "print help")
	flag.BoolVar(&version, "v", false, "print version")
	flag.BoolVar(&version, "version", false, "print version")
	flag.BoolVar(&themes, "themes", false, "print themes")
	flag.StringVar(&comp, "comp", "", "print completion script")
	flag.BoolVar(&raw, "r", false, "treat input as a raw string")
	flag.BoolVar(&slurp, "s", false, "read all inputs into an array")
	flag.BoolVar(&yaml, "yaml", false, "parse input as YAML")
	flag.BoolVar(&toml, "toml", false, "parse input as TOML")
	flag.BoolVar(&strict, "strict", false, "strict mode")
	flag.BoolVar(&noInline, "no-inline", false, "disable inlining in output")
	flag.BoolVar(&gameOfLife, "game-of-life", false, "play the game of life")

	flag.Parse()

	if help {
		printHelp()
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	if version {
		fmt.Println(version)
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	if themes {
		printThemes()
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	if comp != "" {
		printCompletion(comp)
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	if gameOfLife {
		playGameOfLife()
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	// Get input
	var input string
	if len(flag.Args()) > 0 {
		filename := flag.Args()[0]
		data, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n  %s\n  %s\n\n", filename, strings.Repeat("^", len(filename)))
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v\n", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		input = string(data)
	} else {
		// Read from stdin
		buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
		if _, err := io.Copy(buf, os.Stdin); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error reading stdin: %v\n", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		input = buf.String()
	}

	if raw {
		fmt.Println(input)
		os.Exit(0)
	}

	if yaml {
		fmt.Println("YAML not supported")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if toml {
		fmt.Println("TOML not supported")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Parse JSON
	var data interface{}
	if slurp {
		// Slurp mode - read all into array
		decoder := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(input))
		tokens := []interface{}{}
		for {
			tok, err := decoder.Token()
			if err == io.EOF {
				break
			}
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n  %s\n  %s\n\n", "stdin", strings.Repeat("^", 5))
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v\n", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			if tok != nil {
				tokens = append(tokens, tok)
			}
		}
		data = tokens
	} else {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(input), &data); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n  %s\n  %s\n\n", "stdin", strings.Repeat("^", 5))

}

func printThemes() {

		fmt.Println()
	}
}

func printCompletion(shell string) {
	switch shell {
	case "bash":
		fmt.Println("complete -o filenames -C fx fx")
	case "zsh":
		fmt.Println("#compdef fx")
		fmt.Println()
		fmt.Println("_fx() {")
		fmt.Println("    local -a reply")
		fmt.Println("    reply=("${(@f)$(COMP_ZSH=\"${LBUFFER}\" fx)}")")
		fmt.Println("    if (( ${#reply} )); then")
		fmt.Println("        local -a insert_files display_files insert_other display_other")
		fmt.Println("        local line display rest value typ")
		fmt.Println("        ")
		fmt.Println("        for line in \"${reply[@]}\"; do")
		fmt.Println("            display=\"${line%%$'\\t'*}")
		fmt.Println("            rest=\"${line#*$'\\t'}")
		fmt.Println("            value=\"${rest%%$'\\t'*}")
		fmt.Println("            typ=\"${rest#*$'\\t'}")
		fmt.Println()
		fmt.Println("            if [[ \"$typ\" == \"file\" ]]; then")
		fmt.Println("                display_files+=(\"$display\")")
		fmt.Println("                insert_files+=(\"$value\")")
		fmt.Println("            else")
		fmt.Println("                display_other+=(\"$display\")")
		fmt.Println("                insert_other+=(\"$value\")")
		fmt.Println("            fi")
		fmt.Println("        done")
		fmt.Println()
		fmt.Println("        if (( ${#insert_files} )); then")
		fmt.Println("            compadd -f -d display_files -a insert_files")
		fmt.Println("        fi")
		fmt.Println("        if (( ${#insert_other} )); then")
		fmt.Println("            compadd -S '' -d display_other -a insert_other")
		fmt.Println("        fi")
		fmt.Println("    fi")
		fmt.Println("}")
		fmt.Println()
		fmt.Println("if [ \"$funcstack[1]\" = \"_fx\" ]; then")
		fmt.Println("    _fx \"$@\"")
		fmt.Println("else")
		fmt.Println("    compdef _fx fx")
		fmt.Println("fi")
	case "fish":
		fmt.Println("complete --command fx --arguments '(COMP_FISH=(commandline -cp) fx)'")
	default:
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Unknown shell: %s\n", shell)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

}
